campaign.title: AMD MI350X prefill optimization — 5 models x 2 workloads
campaign.hardware: AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950, CDNA4, 256 CU, 287.7 GiB HBM3E), ROCm 7.2 userspace on 7.0.2 host driver

W2.name: 64k ISL at ~93.75% nominal cache hit
W2.note: Nominal 61440/4096 realizes to 67.5k-76.4k depending on tokenizer. Back-solve gsp lengths per model; the achievable hit-rate ceiling is realized-prefix/realized-total and is tokenizer-dependent (90.9%-93.75% measured).

workloads.metric: TTFT (prefill-only; validated equivalent to a dedicated prefill path within 1.5%)

cross_cutting_findings.detail: cc=1 delivers 84.3% (Qwen W1), 90.4% (gpt-oss W1 @cc4), 94% (GLM W1) and 98.5% (Gemma W1) of peak throughput. Going to cc=128 buys 2-6% throughput for ~95-110x the TTFT.
cross_cutting_findings.implication: For prefill-only serving the operating point matters more than any config knob measured. Optimal bands: W1 cc=1-4, W2 cc=8-32.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: Data parallelism beats tensor parallelism for prefill
cross_cutting_findings.detail: 4xTP1 behind a prefix-affinity router: 2.0x TP4's per-GPU throughput AND 2.1x better TTFT uncached; +25% throughput with the best TTFT of any arm cached. Crossover at aggregate cc=2.
cross_cutting_findings.mechanism: TP scales badly: solo 8k prefill is 125.2 ms at TP1, 125.6 ms at TP2 (two GPUs buy nothing), 75.5 ms at TP4 (39-41% efficiency). Dominant cost is shrinking GEMM/MoE tiles, NOT the all-reduce — TP2 with a 2-rank all-reduce is slower per GPU than TP4 with 4 ranks.
cross_cutting_findings.caveat: Round-robin routing instead of prefix-affinity turns the 2x win into a 35% LOSS on cached traffic (hit rate -8.8pt). Affinity balances cleanly only when group count divides replica count.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: Chunk size on cached workloads sets batching WIDTH, not splitting depth
cross_cutting_findings.detail: With ~93% hits only ~4.4k of ~70k tokens per request are new, so chunk governs requests-batched-per-forward-pass. Predictor: requests/pass ~= chunk / new-tokens-per-request. Verified on Qwen (14-16 req/pass in 19 passes at 65536 vs 4-6 in 56 at 16384).
cross_cutting_findings.outcome_is_model_specific: Whether wider batching PAYS depends on how much fixed per-pass cost exists to amortise: Qwen +10.4%, gpt-oss null, GLM -12.1% (per-token DSA cost, nothing fixed to amortise), Gemma a Pareto trade (throughput -7%, TTFT -12.9%).

cross_cutting_findings.finding: Page size is entirely model-specific with four different answers
cross_cutting_findings.detail: gpt-oss requires 64 (1024 costs -18.5% via cache-match granularity); Gemma wants 1 (64 costs -13.5%, 1024 -24.5%, with NO hit-rate loss and NO pool bloat — mechanism unexplained); GLM is forced to 64 and 1024 hangs the server; Qwen cannot exceed 256 (assert mamba_track_interval % page_size == 0).

config_notes: --attention-backend triton MUST be passed alongside the split flags. Omitting it lets the unified value default to aiter, which fires the mem-fraction haircut (0.85 -> 0.7225) and costs 16% of the KV pool.

aiter decode and page_size > 1 only work JOINTLY: aiter decode at page 1 is a -20% regression, page size on triton alone is +0.07%. Page size saturates at 64 (64/128/256 within noise), independently matching vLLM's --block-size=64.

aiter cannot be used as a PREFILL attention backend on this model — no compiled CK instance for its trait tuple (window_size + sink_ptr at head_dim 64). The INT32_MAX/2GB error message is a red herring: a probe with a 410 MB per-layer K buffer, 5x under the stated bound, failed identically.
--prefill-max-requests is a -0.12% no-op here; realized ISL is exactly 8192 (verified three ways), so no sliver exists.
chunk 65536 does NOT win (+0.1-0.96%); saturated at 32768.

build.quickreduce_fix: not applied — shown inert (ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION defaults to NONE, early-returns before init_custom_qr; AiterCustomAllreduce used instead)

tokenizer_provenance.main_sweep: fastokens (upstream). The gigatoken commit 52277afb9c was NOT applied to this build, so --tokenizer-backend gigatoken did not exist.
tokenizer_provenance.dp_experiment: gigatoken (confirmed active in every arm's log)
tokenizer_provenance.issue: The two gpt-oss runs used different tokenizers. Both were verified byte-identical to HF, so token streams and outputs match, but tokenization time lands inside TTFT and fastokens-vs-gigatoken was never A/B'd on this model. For scale: gigatoken took a 15.4k-token prompt from 12.55 ms to 0.16 ms on Qwen, i.e. ~6.5 ms on an 8k prompt or ~9% of gpt-oss's 75.5 ms cc=1 TTFT relative to HF. The fast-vs-fast gap is presumably far smaller but is UNMEASURED.
tokenizer_provenance.impact: Unquantified confound between gpt-oss's main sweep and its DP experiment; cross-model provenance is not tokenizer-uniform.
tokenizer_provenance.recommendation: fastokens is retained in the published config: upstream, requires no patch, verified byte-identical. The inconsistency is a defect in the campaign, not in the config.

W2_hit_rate.why_below_nominal: question inflates 4096 -> 6250 tokens (+53%) while system prompt barely moves; realized ISL 67,560 = 61,310 prefix + 6,250 question

data_parallel.verdict: 4xTP1 + prefix-affinity router is the best configuration on BOTH workloads
notes: Router overhead negligible (+0.14%); all arms ran behind the router so it is common-mode.
Degradation under round-robin is exactly N-fold prefix materialization (1,518,912 lost cached tokens vs 1,474,560 predicted, 3% over).
DP4 gives up 25% of node KV capacity to weight replication but never bound — no retractions or pool-full events in any arm.

caveats: W2 cc1 is the one cell not measured at the intended hit rate (point sizing let it replay the pre-warm's own dataset at 99.91% cached).

models.architecture_note: NOT dense — a 64-layer hybrid: 48 GDN linear-attention + 16 full-attention layers (full_attention_interval 4), head_dim 256, VLM with mrope. Only 1 layer in 4 holds KV, hence the 6.67M token pool.
config_notes: --max-prefill-tokens MUST be raised with the chunk or the 16384 default binds (~2.7%). Flag semantics: raising above chunk is inert; lowering below chunk binds but does NOT collapse to the equivalent chunk's behaviour.
mem_fraction_static 0.85 resolves to 0.7225 here (aiter + context > 8192). max_total_num_tokens ~6.67M.
--page-size 1024 is structurally impossible: assert mamba_track_interval % page_size == 0, and mamba_track_interval defaults to 256. Hybrid-model-only constraint.
Prefill/decode backend split is worth +0.1% — nothing at OSL=1.
The tuned GEMM table must be a8w8_blockscale_bpreshuffle, NOT plain a8w8_blockscale, and must be extended to M=65536 (3456 -> 3540 rows, 135/135 probe hits).

build.method: git apply -3 of individual feature commits

W2.note: realized ISL 70,109 = 65,726.6 system + 4,382.9 question; inflation proportional so ratio stays 93.75%. in_tok_s counts CACHED tokens and is inflated ~16x — true new-token rate at cc=32 is 28,435 tok/s.

open_issues: 776 bf16 (not fp8) GEMM misses at M=65536,N=24,K=5120 — untuned shape in bf16_tuned_gemm.csv, present on all chunk-65536 arms
models.drift: +0.88% (cc32) / -0.23% (cc8) over ~50 min under contention; replicate spread 1.0-1.1% (W2), 0.14-1.5% (W1)

config_notes: --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable is the DEFAULT and CRASHES GLM-5.2 on ROCm, so the model does not start out of the box. tc_piecewise fails identically; full fails differently (DeepseekSparseAttnBackend missing decode_cuda_graph_metadata). Only disabled works.
If one config must serve both workloads use chunk 32768: it costs W1 ~2-3%, whereas 16384 costs W2 ~11% at cc8.
mem_fraction_static 0.85 takes NO aiter haircut (backend resolves to dsa) — 0.8597 of 287.69 GiB used, KV 145.83 GB, max_total_num_tokens 1,563,392.

--max-prefill-tokens is NEVER inert; it resolves literally even at context_len=1048576. But its semantics are a BATCH-WIDTH limiter, not a chunking limiter: at mpt=4096 a single 8192-token request is still admitted whole. Chunking is governed solely by chunked_prefill_size.

--page-size is forced to 64 (sglang logs 'Setting page size to 64 for DeepSeek DSA'). Passing 1024 is actively harmful: it perturbs memory sizing (max_total_num_tokens 595,072 vs 1,563,392) and HUNG the server into a watchdog kill. The override reaches the attention path but not the memory-pool path — a real bug.
Tight --context-length buys 14 GB free VRAM and max_running_requests 4096 vs 2048.

build.model: zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 (756 GB, 141 shards), GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM, 78 layers + 1 MTP, MLA kv_lora_rank 512, DSA index_topk 2048, 256 experts / 8 active

W2_chunk_ladder_tok_s.note: hit-rate control PASSED — server-side 93.69% identical on all three rungs

mechanism.conclusion: GLM's DSA prefill cost is PER-TOKEN, not per-pass — there is nothing fixed to amortise, plus a superlinear penalty above ~32768 tokens/pass
mechanism.evidence_1: batching width matched the predictor exactly (W2 chunk/4311 + ~1 -> 5/9/16 observed, passes 136->69->35)
mechanism.evidence_2: per-pass time is proportional to tokens-per-pass: W1 cc128 819/1665/3331 ms (2.03x, 2.00x); W2 cc128 1229/2447/5434 ms (1.99x, 2.22x)
mechanism.evidence_3: --max-prefill-tokens 4096 collapsed width 5->1 and passes 33->128 (3.9x more passes) for a cost of only -1.84%

models.drift: concentrated at high concurrency: -5.5% at cc128, -4.9% at cc32, but -0.26%/+0.07% at cc1/cc8 over 2h43m. Cross-boot comparisons at cc32/cc128 need >5.5% margins.

config.TVM_FFI_CACHE_DIR: REQUIRED — server dies at ~55 s without it

config_notes: --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable CRASHES Gemma4 (ValueError: You must specify exactly one of input_ids or inputs_embeds). sglang AUTO-DISABLES the prefill graph for this multimodal arch; passing the flag OVERRIDES that auto-disable and re-enables a broken path.
Prefill/decode backend split is ILLEGAL: 'Gemma4 only supports trtllm_mha, triton, or intel_xpu attention backend'. gpt-oss's +18.3% cannot transfer.
--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion is INERT — zero allreduce_fusion call sites in any gemma4*.py.
--prefill-max-requests 4 gains +1.3% throughput / -2.1% TTFT at cc>=32 despite realized ISL being exactly 8192, because the scheduler otherwise packs a 5th partial request (#new-seq: 5). W1-specific.

--swa-full-tokens-ratio: KEEP the 0.8 default. Lowering it scales the pool hugely (0.3 -> 1.35M, 0.15 -> 2.16M full-layer tokens) but is a clear loss (cc32: 37.1k vs 61.0k tok/s) — the SWA pool is the binding constraint and SWA tokens cost ~10x full-pool tokens (191 KB vs 19 KB).

not_applicable_confirmed: JIT NDEBUG (python/sglang/kernels/jit/ does not exist in 0.5.16)

W1.note: server-verified 0.00% cached, 512/512, 0 errors. Throughput flat within +/-3.5% while TTFT scales exactly linearly (412 ms x cc).
W1.mechanism: server batch width is chunk/ISL = 4-5 regardless of client cc; full_tok_usage peaks at 0.07 — W1 never touches the KV pool

W2.note: corrected protocol: constant ppg=32, per-rung flush; hit 90.2-90.9% every rung

chunk_ladder.conclusion: batching-width mechanism reproduces exactly (2.7x fewer passes) but does NOT buy throughput — 65536 is 7% slower. Only TTFT p50 improves monotonically (-12.9%). A genuine Pareto trade, unlike Qwen. Matches the prediction: with 50/60 sliding layers at window 1024, only 10 layers walk the long prefix, so there is little per-pass cost to amortise.

page_size_ladder_W2_tok_s.note: hit-matched, pool flat. Gemma lost NO hit rate at any page size (90.5-91.3% at cc32), so this is NOT cache-match granularity (unlike gpt-oss) and NOT pool bloat. Mechanism unexplained; penalty grows with concurrency.

capacity_finding.headline: Group count decides W2 throughput by 3.05x
capacity_finding.detail: Realized 8 x 71.6k prefixes = 573k against a 599k pool produced a cyclic-LRU cliff: 6 x 76k prompts all retained, 8 x 76k retained 0/8. As-briefed 8-group W2 runs at 82.1% hit / 37,100 tok/s versus calibrated 4-group 113,292 tok/s at cc=128.
capacity_finding.rule: Keep the prefix working set under ~250k tokens

models.drift: W1 replicated within +/-0.2% across 2.9 hours. W2 noisier: +/-1.8% at cc128/cc32 but -15% at cc8 — trust W2 cc>=16, treat W2 cc<=8 deltas as noise.
models.tokenizer_note: gigatoken encode byte-identical to HF on all edge cases and every W1/W2 prompt. Its decode diverges only on runs of >=2 adjacent <0xNN> byte-fallback tokens (HF emits one U+FFFD each, gigatoken assembles bytes) — irrelevant here since the client tokenizes with HF and OSL=1.

known_constraints: W4A16 only — MXFP4 is ~7.5x faster but costs 2.2 pp gsm8k AND vLLM #36337 reports gibberish on MI350X/ROCm 7.2 (our exact stack)
gigatoken cannot load a TikToken tokenizer — fails loudly
Structural ceiling: CDNA4 has no native INT4, so W4A16 runs at the bf16 dequant ceiling (~2,632 tok/s/GPU measured previously)

gfx950 Triton MoE table is a PARTIAL hit: up-projection resolves, down-projection reports 'Down MoE config file not found', and 'Using default MoE kernel config' NEVER appears — the usual grep misleads
SWA / prefix-trim changes are inert (routes through AITER MLA, triton extend_attention compiles: 0)
models.prediction: Chunk behaviour closer to Qwen (AITER MLA with no sliding window walks the full cached prefix every layer = maximum fixed per-pass cost to amortise), UNLESS memory caps batching width first — the likely binding constraint on the largest model.

prior_measurements_to_confirm_or_refute.note: the cached 64k prompt was FASTER than an uncached 8k one

mandatory_flags.--random-range-ratio: 1.0 — the default 0.0 gives a mean of ~50% of nominal ISL and P99 +357%
mandatory_flags.--disable-radix-cache: on the SERVER for uncached work; distinct prompts are not enough

W2_protocol: Pin the seed across prewarm and measurement
Keep --gsp-prompts-per-group CONSTANT between prewarm and measurement (ppg-invariance is partial: ppg=1 vs ppg=16 prefix sets matched 8/8 for a fixed seed, but ppg=4 vs ppg=1 did not)
flush_cache before EVERY point — descending ladders otherwise re-run the previous rung's exact requests (observed 100.0% hit, 17 new tokens, 651k tok/s = void data)
Back-solve gsp lengths so REALIZED ISL lands near the target; nominal 61440/4096 realizes to 67.5k-76.4k depending on tokenizer
Size group count so the prefix working set fits the KV pool — 8 groups overflowed Gemma's and retained 0/8
Discriminating control for whether prewarm works: same ppg with a NON-matching seed. Only discriminates at low ppg; at ppg>=32 amortization and prewarm predictions converge.
reporting: Report realized ISL and the computed hit-rate ceiling (realized-prefix / realized-total), not the nominal 93.75%
Quote per-point steady-state hit rate, not the whole-log aggregate (87.9% vs 93.7% on the same run — two denominators)
in_tok/s on cached workloads counts cached tokens and is inflated ~16x — report the true new-token rate separately
Exclude ttft = 0.0 records but report the fraction excluded
#running-req is NOT residency — it tracks cumulative requests processed. Use full_tok_usage and #new-seq; label concurrency client-offered
Include a drift control and state the contention boundary
operational_traps: ufw limit ssh is active — retries REFRESH the block. Use one ssh ControlMaster socket; detach long runs with nohup setsid
Never pattern-kill (pkill -f launch_server matches every agent's server AND your own shell). Kill by port: ss -ltnpH sport = :PORT -> PGID
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES REPLACES a container's GPU restriction rather than intersecting it — use --base-gpu-id on restricted containers
docker ps is blind to k3s pods — judge occupancy from rocm-smi --showmeminfo vram --csv in BYTES, never --showmemuse
The AOT build tracks no header dependencies — editing a .cuh yields a stale .so that runs cleanly and silently gives unpatched results
--enable-cache-report defaults off on the server on some builds (gpt-oss needed it; GLM and Gemma reported hit rates without it) — verify rather than assume

open_issues: MI355X: 32 idle GPUs on mi355x-amd-slurm, unreachable — the slurm jumpbox at 216.114.73.93 rejects both available SSH keys. Needs an ops request.

Upstream PR correction needed: QuickReduce is inert on most images (ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION defaults to NONE and early-returns), so the 'shipped default' framing overstates the defect. It WAS set to INT8 by the image where the bug was found — the defect is real but image-dependent.
Unfiled bug: GLM --page-size 1024 hangs the server; the override reaches the attention path but not the memory-pool path.
Unfiled bug: prefill CUDA graphs are broken on ROCm for DSA models (GLM) and are wrongly re-enabled by the flag on multimodal models (Gemma).
Branch commit f25dca3f6f (DSA in-graph prefill HIP port) is UNVALIDATED on hardware — GLM's campaign ran entirely on disabled.
Qwen: 776 bf16 GEMM misses at M=65536,N=24,K=5120 — untuned shape in bf16_tuned_gemm.csv.

Tokenizer provenance is not uniform across the campaign: gpt-oss's main sweep used fastokens, while its DP experiment and the other three models used gigatoken. Both were verified byte-identical to HF; the TTFT impact of fastokens vs gigatoken is unmeasured.
